chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hammad ibn Abi Talha (or Abu) Talha, the seller of Sabir, and Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, and Hakim al-Hannat, all together from Abu Hamza, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever withholds the wealth of a Muslim man, while he is able to give it to him, fearing that if that right were to go out from his hand he would be impoverished, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more able to impoverish him than he is to annihilate himself by withholding that right.'

key_terms.مَخَافَةَ: fearing or out of fear of

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of withholding a debt out of fear of poverty?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the psychological barrier of 'fear of poverty' is corrected by the theological principle of divine sufficiency (Kifayah), emphasizing that Allah’s power to provide or deprive far exceeds human capacity. This hadith serves as a cornerstone for the etiquette of debt repayment in Shia jurisprudence, urging believers to prioritize fulfilling rights over material accumulation, trusting in Allah’s promise that He will not let the righteous lack sustenance. It highlights the spiritual danger of hoarding wealth due to misplaced trust in one's own resources rather than Divine decree.
